title: Longest Valid Parentheses Substring
statement: You are given a string s containing only the characters '(' and ')'. A substring is 'balanced' if it is a contiguous slice of s that forms a properly matched parentheses sequence (every '(' is later closed by a matching ')', and every ')' closes an earlier '('). Return the length of the longest balanced contiguous substring of s as an integer. Substrings must be contiguous: characters that match across a gap do not count. If no balanced substring exists (including when s is empty), return 0.
hints: Instead of asking about any substring, ask a narrower question at each position: what is the length of the longest balanced substring that ENDS exactly at index i? Can that be built from answers for earlier indices?

Keep dp[i] = length of the longest balanced substring ending at i. Only a ')' can close a run. If s[i-1] is '(', you just closed an adjacent pair, so dp[i] = dp[i-2] + 2. Otherwise s[i-1] is ')' and you must jump BACK over the already-valid block of length dp[i-1] to reach the potential matching '(' at index i - dp[i-1] - 1.

When s[i]==')' and s[i-1]==')': let j = i - dp[i-1] - 1. If j >= 0 and s[j]=='(', then that '(' matches the current ')', wrapping the inner block, so dp[i] = dp[i-1] + 2, and you must also add the block ending just before j: dp[i] += dp[j-1] when j >= 1. Track the running maximum of dp[i]; return 0 if nothing balanced was found.
